articles.title_orig: Stock Market Today: Dow Opens Lower; Apple Stock Falls After Earnings Disappoint
articles.title_zh: Stock Market Today: Dow Opens Lower; Apple Stock Falls After Earnings Disappoint
articles.content_orig:
Bill Ackman told CNBC on Tuesday he worries that the stock market is broken, saying the rise of speculative trading is leading to wild price swings thanks to the amount of leverage in the system.
"Every number of days, I feel like markets are broken," Ackman said on CNBC's " Squawk Box ." "Stocks trade at prices that make no sense to me. Yes, it's good if you're a long-term investor and you can buy at a stupid price. I don't think it's good for the country generally."
"We're back to the casino-type markets when there was 95% leverage," he added. "I don't think that's inherently good for the economy, for society, and it's leading to these massive moves in stocks."
The founder of Pershing Square Capital Management said those same dislocations in the market have given the hedge fund the opportunity to snag big bargains.
Pershing bought Microsoft , for example, when it was pummeled during the "SaaSpocalypse" earlier this year, and Amazon when it fell following President Donald Trump's tariffs, Ackman said. It also bought Alphabet when the stock moved "massively" following ChatGPT's launch, he said.
But the billionaire investor worries that the rise of one-day leveraged vehicles, perpetual futures and sports betting is dangerous for investors who are treating the stock market as a get-rich-quick scheme — an attitude that could have disastrous consequences.
"It's good for us long term — 'us' being Pershing Square," he said. "I don't think it's good for the country."
Among the stocks Ackman is especially bullish on are Visa and Mastercard , which he called among the world's "greatest" businesses, as well as streaming platform Netflix, in which he disclosed a position in August.

articles.title_orig: Death toll hits 31 after Russian strikes on a Ukrainian aid site, with dozens still missing
articles.title_zh: Death toll hits 31 after Russian strikes on a Ukrainian aid site, with dozens still missing
articles.content_orig:
In this photo provided by the Ukrainian Emergency Service, rescuers evacuate a wounded civilian from a residential building after Russian air attack in Dnipro, Ukraine, Tuesday, Nov. 3, 2026. Ukrainian Emergency Service/via AP hide caption
KYIV, Ukraine — The death toll from a Russian attack in southern Ukraine on a site where people had gathered to receive humanitarian aid rose to 29 on Tuesday, with 48 still missing, as a wave of overnight strikes targeted power plants across the country, damaged hospitals and wounded scores of people.
Dozens of rescuers and volunteers continued to search the cratered blast site of a destroyed aid facility and shelter in Komyushuvakha, a village in Ukraine's southern Zaporizhzhia region, hoping to find missing residents alive under the rubble. Instead, more bodies were pulled out and carried away in white plastic sheeting.
"The scale of the tragedy is terrifying," Mykhailo Semikin, acting head of the region's military administration, wrote in an online post. "This is one of the worst tragedies in terms of the number of civilian victims in our region since the start of the full-scale war."
A woman and her cat take shelter from a Russian drone and missile attack, in a metro station, now used as a bomb shelter, in Kyiv, Ukraine, Tuesday, Nov. 3, 2026. Danylo Antoniuk/AP hide caption
Russia launched 289 attack drones, 17 ballistic missiles and 59 cruise missiles across nine regions, triggering emergency power cuts, President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said in an online post that noted the barrage coincided with U.S. elections.
"The Russians think America won't notice this signal of theirs," he said. "But we need to notice and stop such terror. We need to help Ukraine defend its skies; otherwise, Russia will never stop its missile strikes."
Three days of mourning were declared in Zaporizhzhia where Russian bunker-busting bombs, filled with nearly 1.5 tons of explosives, were used in Monday's attack.
The dead included four police officers and two rescue workers, Semikin said Tuesday. At least five people were hurt.
In this photo provided by the Ukrainian Emergency Service, a residential building is seen following a Russian air attack in Dnipro, Ukraine, Tuesday, Nov. 3, 2026. Ukrainian Emergency Service/via AP hide caption
In the northeast region of Kharkiv, a combined Russian missile and drone attack wounded at least 62 people, local authorities said.
A strike damaged a medical facility in the Nemyshlianskyi district, shattered windows in four apartment buildings and damaged cars. More than 200 patients were transferred to other medical facilities, head of the regional military administration Oleh Syniehubov said.
In the Dnipro area, rescuers pulled a woman alive from the rubble Tuesday morning, after a Russian attack killed one person and wounded 17, local authorities said.
The attack damaged an outpatient clinic and a hospital. Patients were transferred to other hospitals, Oleksandr Hanzha, head of the regional military administration, said.
Russia's Ministry of Defense said Tuesday that it had shot down 856 Ukrainian drones overnight. Moscow mayor Sergei Sobyanin said 493 drones were fired toward the Russian capital.
A Ukrainian drone attack wounded two employees at an oil refinery in the Russian city of Yaroslavl, regional Gov. Mikhail Yevrayev said Tuesday. He added that there was damage to the refinery's infrastructure.
Rolling blackouts have been instituted in the south, west and east of Russian-occupied Crimea following attacks on energy infrastructure, Moscow-installed officials said Tuesday.

articles.title_orig: Palantir Stock Tumbles as Wall Street Finds Problems in Big Earnings Beat
articles.title_zh: Palantir Stock Tumbles as Wall Street Finds Problems in Big Earnings Beat
articles.content_orig:
Palantir shares fell on Tuesday after the software company reported third-quarter earnings and analysts pointed to signs of a slowdown in total contract value and other "forward indicators."
U.S. commercial revenue topped government for the first time, but the company closed $1.5 billion in TCV in the segment, up 11% from last year. In Q2, Palantir closed a record $2.1 billion worth of TCV in the segment, which was up 153% from the prior year.
Investors will "no doubt be looking for evidence in subsequent quarters that 11% growth in U.S. commercial TCV bookings is a fluke of duration and not something structural," a Piper Sandler note from Monday said. "We believe that is the case and demand for PLTR's solutions still very much outstrip supply."
In a Tuesday note, Goldman Sachs analysts noted that the company attributed some of this to shorter contract durations.
"The key will be converting shorter duration contracts into longer duration commitments, which Palantir has done successfully in the past," the analysts wrote.
Revenue nearly doubled from a year ago and blew past $2 billion for the first time, Palantir said in its earnings report.
The iPhone maker reported better-than-expected revenue in its fourth-quarter earnings, but fell short of estimates on iPad sales and issued a margin forecast that disappointed investors.
Apple 's statement marked the first earnings report since John Ternus took over as CEO from Tim Cook in September. The stock fell more than 2% on Tuesday.
The company is reckoning with a global memory crunch and a scramble for computer components. Memory costs were higher this quarter than in the June period, the company said Monday. Despite the price surge, Ternus said Apple had just capped off its "best fiscal year ever."
He told CNBC's MacKenzie Sigalos that Apple's growth came despite supply constraints and foreign exchange headwinds.
"The concern is profitability," said Violeta Todorova, senior research analyst at Leverage Shares. "Management pointed to memory as the main pressure, together with the cost of rolling out Siri AI. Memory shortages are also expected to limit Mac and iPad supply, as demand has run ahead of plans."
Apple shares have risen 25% in 2026, ahead of other big tech names, but that premium leaves "little room for disappointment," Todorova added.

articles.title_orig: NATO’s New Defense Plan Would Mean Strikes Deep Inside Russia
articles.title_zh: NATO’s New Defense Plan Would Mean Strikes Deep Inside Russia
articles.content_orig:
Admiral Rob Bauer, former Chair of the NATO Military Committee, expressed this view in an interview with Ukrinform on the sidelines of a special event organized by the Brussels office of the Kyiv Security Forum.
"Ukraine has to fight this war in a certain way because it was limited by the U.S. and other Western nations in the use of certain weapon systems or not allowed to use some of them. So NATO is not going to fight exactly the same way as Ukraine is fighting the Russians," Bauer said.
He explained that in the event of an attack, the Alliance would deploy its air force and navy and launch long-range precision strikes against Russian territory.
"This is something that Ukraine is now doing more and more with weapon systems that it has developed yourself. As you were limited at the outset, you started to work on the drones. So in a way, the drones were your answer to a limited amount of artillery ammo. The fact that you are successful in that area now is a testament to the fact that you found an answer to the fact that you were not supported as we should have supported you," the admiral said.
Even Ukraine's possession of a certain number of F-16 fighter jets cannot match the capabilities of a full fleet of strategic bombers, F-35s, F-22s, F-15s, F-16s and other assets available to the Alliance, Bauer said.
He added that the Alliance's regional plans are fully aligned with the tasks at hand.
"General Grynkewich, NATO's SACEUR, talked about this at a forum in Warsaw just a couple of weeks ago. His message was that Article 5 is ironclad and that the U.S forces in Europe will fight within NATO to first block the Russians, then blunt them if necessary, and if it takes longer, to break them. We are talking about the industrial complex and the logistics support of a longer war that we will have to break, as Ukraine is doing now with Russia, with its refineries and everything else," the admiral said.
Asked whether he believed all NATO allies would have the political will to repel an aggressor, Bauer said: "General Grynkewich would never have been able to say this in Warsaw if it hadn't been exclusively approved by the White House."
In Bauer's view, this was "a message from President Trump to NATO: America is with NATO, article 5 is ironclad, and the regional plans are in place."
He also explained that if intelligence indicated Russia was building up its forces and the Alliance knew which direction they might try to advance in, "the battle groups can be strengthened from 1,000 to 5,000, to a brigade size in different nations."
"At the political level, these plans have already been agreed, so at a certain stage, within those plans, certain things are going to happen," the admiral said.
He added that the situation had been different in the past, when many of these measures would have been debated, with questions raised about whether they were necessary.

articles.title_orig: 5 people rescued in South Pacific after months adrift at sea, 4 others missing
articles.title_zh: 5 people rescued in South Pacific after months adrift at sea, 4 others missing
articles.content_orig:
Five people, including two children, were rescued this week in the South Pacific island nation of Kiribati after three months drifting at sea in a 20-foot skiff, authorities said. Another four remained missing.
Villagers rescued the group Sunday off Fanning Island in Kiribati, the Australian Broadcasting Corp. reported , after they had drifted an estimated 3,355 miles east from the Federated States of Micronesia.
The U.S. Coast Guard in Guam on Tuesday confirmed that the skiff with nine people aboard had been reported missing after it failed to return to Ruo Island in Micronesia on July 30. The group had been making a one-hour crossing between the islands of Murilo and Ruo at the time, ABC reported.
A 10-day search covering 33,000 square miles followed without any sign of the missing boat or those aboard, it said.
"Incredible and wonderful news these five folks were found and are receiving care," the U.S. Coast Guard told The Associated Press in an email.
"Our profound condolences to family and friends of those who did not arrive with them," the email added.
When asked by the AP what happened to the missing four, the U.S. Coast Guard said it was continuing to gather and confirm information and would reply as soon as possible.
A lawmaker in Kiribati, Kaotitaake Rakoroa, told ABC the survivors were being cared for by a pastor on the island.
Nursing officer Paukin Tororo told the ABC on Monday that all five were severely dehydrated and malnourished. They were put on intravenous drips and were showing signs of recovery.
"They can give a smile face, they show the sign they want to eat," she told the ABC.
The survivors had yet to speak publicly about their ordeal and had requested privacy, the Australian broadcaster reported. ABC said the group went missing after their boat was caught in a storm.
The governor of Micronesia's Chuuk state, Alexander Narruhn, issued a statement Sunday saying he had begun talks with the Kiribati government to bring the survivors home.
"There were nine people aboard the boat that went missing. Thanks be to God for his love and mercy that five of the nine have been found," Narruhn said through an interpreter.
"We continue to pray for their four companions," he added. Narruhn did not immediately respond to the AP's request for comment.
There have been previous incidents where people have become lost at sea among the tiny island chains that stud the Pacific Ocean. An Australian man survived more than two months lost at sea in 2023 with his dog Bella after rough seas damaged their boat and its electronics system. Tim Shaddock, 51, had been traveling from Mexico to French Polynesia, but found himself drifting in the Pacific Ocean for more than two months. Shaddock and his canine companion survived by drinking rain water and eating raw fish that Shaddock caught, he said. They were spotted by a helicopter and rescued in July 2023.
Two American sailors and their two dogs were rescued after five months at sea in the Pacific in 2017. Jennifer Appel and Tasha Fuiaba were discovered 900 miles southeast of Japan by a Taiwanese fishing ship, the U.S. Navy said at the time. The vessel's engine died during bad weather, and they were unable to get to land using the ship's sails. The women said the boat drifted off course, and no ships were near enough to hear their distress calls. Water purifiers and a year's supply of food aboard the vessel kept them alive, the Navy said.
In 2024, three fishermen were stranded on a remote Micronesian island for more than a week . They were rescued after using palm leaves to spell out "HELP" in large letters on a beach.

Firstly, the download size for GTA 6 is a max of 212GB . Rockstar says that this may change "depending on your device", but you'll want to make sure you have at least 212GB of spare storage just in case.
Meanwhile, preloading begins for Xbox Series X|S on November 10th at 12am GMT .

In addition to this, the release time for GTA 6 has been confirmed as "midnight local time" on November 19th, which means some people will be getting access to it earlier than others depending on where in the world they reside.
Another last little bit of new information today is that a poster of the GTA 6 artwork and map will be made available to download for free at launch, or you'll be able to buy a physical version for $0.99 if you prefer.

articles.content_orig:
Seven bomb threats have now been reported across Europe, all incidents have been confirmed as false alarms
Bringing it all together, seven bomb threats have now been reported in total:
LOT Polish Airlines flight from London Heathrow, UK to Warsaw Okęcie, diverted to Warsaw Modlin, Poland ( 10:33 , 10:58 , 12:00 , 13:57 ).
SAS flight from Copenhagen, Denmark to Warsaw Okęcie ( 11:33 , 12:59 ).
Ryanair flight from Manchester, UK to Murcia, Spain ( 12:44 , 13:44 )
Ryanair flight from Lisbon, Portugal to Rome, Italy ( 15:02 )
Ryanair flight from Dublin, Ireland to Rome, Italy
WizzAir flight from Bergamo, Italy to Sofia, Bulgaria ( 15:41 )
Ryanair flight from Dublin, Ireland to Sofia, Bulgaria
All seven have been confirmed to be false alarms.
It’s also worth recalling some other similar incidents in the last few weeks.
On 18 October, an Austrian Airlines flight from Tel Aviv to ​Vienna diverted to Sofia ‌after a reported bomb ​threat while over Romania, Reuters said.
And yesterday, on 2 November, a WizzAir flight from London to Sofia was diverted to Budapest after a bomb threat ( 10:44 ).
Reuters is carrying a quick confirmation that the flight from Bergamo to Sofia in Bulgaria was operated by WizzAir, not Ryanair.
This has also been updated in the tally at the top of the page.

There is also an update from Bulgaria, with the country’s transport ministry telling Reuters the bomb threats were actually made against two planes from Bergamo in Italy and Dublin in Ireland, and not from Israel as previously reported.
That brings the total to seven planes (that we know of).
Back to Berlin, Ukraine’s Zelenskyy also rejects Russia’s suggestion of a meeting in Moscow as “counterproductive.” He says what’s needed is serious talks, and not a gimmick.
He also insists that Russia has no advantage on the frontline at the moment.
Merz then adds that the 19 November meeting will decide further support for Ukraine in 2027 , and that concludes the press.
Meanwhile, two more false bomb threats were reported in Italy involving Ryanair flights from Lisbon and Dublin to Rome’s Fiumicino Airport, according to the Italian newspapers La Repubblica and Corriere della Sera.
The plane from Dublin was escorted by two Italian air force fighter jets, newspaper reported.
In both cases, routine checks were confirmed as negative, meaning no threat was identified, SkyTG24 said.
That brings the total of flights affected by false alarms today to at least six, up from four reported earlier (that we know of).
Asked about his expectations for the Abu Dhabi talks, Zelenskyy says he hopes to see future security guarantees for Ukraine to be covered, alongside a “prosperity package” that would help with the reconstruction of Ukraine.
He also says he hopes to discuss a proposal on energy, Black Sea truce, which is “in the interest of not only Ukraine, but also Russia and various nations in Africa.”
He reiterates that “there can be no stable peace unless Europe is at the negotiating table.”
Merz for his part says that “it is crucial for Russia to finally engage in serious negotiations.”
Responding, Zelenskyy thanks Germany for its continued help, including on air defence, and says that while many people will be following the events in the US today’s midterm elections, “the role of Europe – and specifically Germany – remains crucial.”
He says he briefed Merz on the latest attacks on Ukraine .
He also confirms the upcoming Abu Dhabi talks on 10-11 November ( 11:21 ) , which he says hopefully “will pave the way for a trilateral meeting at the level of heads of states and government.”
He also confirms further talks on Ukraine will be held in Brussels on Wednesday ( 12:41 ), as per the European Commission’s announcement earlier, and that the coalition of the willing will meet in Berlin on 19 November.
Germany’s Merz begins by saying Zelenskyy’s visit comes “at a critical moment” as Russian attacks on Ukraine continued with “undiminished – indeed, increasing – severity and ruthlessness.”
He says Ukraine “can continue to rely on Germany,” with more support from Berlin in the coming months, including on air defence, energy, and broader winter-related aid.
Merz also warns that the outcome of the war in Ukraine “will determine European security for a long time to come.”
He says Germany will be coordinating with France and the UK, and will host a meeting of the Coalition of the Willing in Berlin later this month.
The German chancellor also talks of growing concerns about the broader effects of the continuing war, including a potential “global food crisis” triggered by Russia’s continued attacks on trading routes in the Black Sea.
He says the upcoming Abu Dhabi talks are “the right step forward,” and Europe hopes to play its part.
In the meantime, Berlin and partners will “increase the pressure on Moscow and continue to support Ukraine,” he says.
Meanwhile, Germany’s Merz and Ukraine’s Zelenskyy are now briefing the media after their talks in Berlin.
I will bring you the key lines here.
Similarly, Warsaw-Modlin Airport has also given the all-clear after concluding security sweeps on a LOT Polish Airlines flight from London Heathrow following an earlier bomb alert ( 10:33 ).
“The bomb threat was called off … Following the completion of operations by the relevant services, Warsaw/Modlin Airport has returned to normal functioning.”
We have just got an update from Spain’s Guardia Civil on the Ryanair flight from Manchester to Murcia ( 12:44 ).
The authorities “ruled out the presence of explosives on the plane,” the Spanish government’s delegate in the region of Murcia, Francisco Lucas , confirmed .
“The International Airport of the Region of Murcia resumes its activity normally. Thanks to the emergency teams that have participated in the operation,” he said.
Over in Sweden , centrist leader Elisabeth Thand Ringqvist has just lost a vote on her proposed government – which is hardly surprising given that even she as very clear she had no chance of winning.
324 votes against, 25 in favour.
It’s been 51 days since the Swedish parliamentary election, and it’s the second failed attempt to form the government. Two more and we get a snap election. Gulp.
The next attempt is expected to be led by the interim centre-right prime minister, Ulf Kristersson, but his outgoing coalition is also unlikely to secure enough support in the parliament, further complicating the process.
Here are some more photos from Berlin where Zelenskyy is now taking part in talks with Merz ( 11:53 ).
If you are joining us now, we are following reports about at least four planes affected by bomb threats across Europe this morning : two in Poland (from the UK 10:33 , 10:58 , 12:00 and Denmark 11:33 , 12:59 ), one in Bulgaria (from Israel 12:50 ), and one in Spain (from the UK 12:44 ).
All four of them landed safely and are being checked by security services. It may be nothing, but is highly unusual (particularly after another alert yesterday 10:44 ), so we are keeping a close eye on that.
Separately, we are keeping an eye on Berlin where Ukraine’s president Volodymyr Zelenskyy is just arriving to meet German chancellor Friedrich Merz on his previously unannounced high-security trip to Berlin.
We should hear from them in the next hour or so.

articles.title_orig: SpaceX and Musk Have Big Wireless Ambitions. Boost Mobile Won’t Fulfill Them.
articles.title_zh: SpaceX and Musk Have Big Wireless Ambitions. Boost Mobile Won’t Fulfill Them.
articles.content_orig:
Oops, something went wrong
SpaceX ( SPCX ) may be attempting an end run to circumvent obstacles it's facing in getting a mobile network off the ground.
Per the Washington Post , SpaceX is in talks with EchoStar ( SATS ) about launching its own wireless phone service through Boost Mobile, after the country's three biggest carriers — Verizon, AT&T ( T ), and T-Mobile ( TMUS ) — reportedly turned down SpaceX CEO Elon Musk.
Musk met with EchoStar chairman Charlie Ergen last month, according to two people familiar with the negotiations cited by the Post. The talks could end with SpaceX buying Boost Mobile outright or getting access to its network, which the discount carrier leases from AT&T and T-Mobile.
In recent months, Musk asked the heads of Verizon ( VZ ), AT&T and T-Mobile to let SpaceX use their networks for its own mobile service. All three said no, per the Post.
But there may be a catch to SpaceX's plan. Typically, a carrier's lease agreement can't be transferred to a new owner without the host carrier's permission, meaning AT&T and T-Mobile may still need to approve a Boost deal to provide access to SpaceX.
SpaceX is open about its ambitions in the terrestrial mobile space. On the company's recent earnings call , CFO Bret Johnsen said the goal is to "become a major mobile carrier ... in the United States." SpaceX also recently agreed to buy $8 billion worth of wireless spectrum licenses intended for cellular service in places satellites can't reach.
"This is the last critical piece of the spectrum puzzle needed for SpaceX to provide complete phone coverage in America," Musk said on X .
SpaceX and EchoStar already have a relationship. In September 2025, SpaceX agreed to buy EchoStar's AWS-4 and H-block spectrum licenses for about $17 billion, split between up to $8.5 billion in cash and up to $8.5 billion in SpaceX stock, EchoStar said at the time . SpaceX President Gwynne Shotwell said the deal would "advance our mission to end mobile dead zones."
What SpaceX still lacks is a ground network. Its satellite signal isn't strong enough yet to carry cell coverage indoors or in dense cities, where most phones are - and that's why a deal with Boost would be so crucial.
An MVNO (mobile virtual network operator) like Boost rents capacity on an existing carrier's network. Last month, TD Cowen's Gregory Williams called acquiring an MVNO the cheapest and fastest route for SpaceX to launch mobile service, noting a network build would cost "upwards of $80B" and take years.
The Big 3, he said, still show no desire "to (ever) sign an MVNO deal with Starlink that could ravage the industry."
Carrier executives have publicly doubted that SpaceX can rebuild their tower networks. Verizon's CEO put the build-out at four to six years. Musk said it would take about half that.
"Veterans of the cellular industry look at the chess board of existing pieces and don't see a solution," Musk said recently on X . "They don't understand that SpaceX is developing entirely new pieces that fundamentally alter the strategic landscape."

articles.title_orig: ‘Dead By Daylight’ Strips TheBurntPeanut’s Content, Apologizes To No Avail
articles.title_zh: ‘Dead By Daylight’ Strips TheBurntPeanut’s Content, Apologizes To No Avail
articles.content_orig:
Dead by Daylight studio Behaviour Interactive has apologised for a recent incident in which it appeared to gift an offensive streamer free content while acknowledging and dismissing the complaints it would receive.
TheBurntPeanut, who has a reputation online for being a deliberately provocative streamer who regularly uses homophobic and other slurs in their streams, was awarded a large helping of paid DLC (reportedly around $300 worth) for free during a stream.
Players complained that Behaviour appeared to be rewarding someone whose content goes against the Dead by Daylight community’s ethos of inclusivity.
This was exacerbated on the game’s official Discord server when TheBurntPeanut offered to step away, saying: “If you don’t want people on Twitter to be upset, I’ll take the heat and you can take away the DLC.”
Instead, a team member, posting under the official DeadByDaylight account, replied in all caps: “WE CAN TAKE THE HEAT! THEY ARE YOURS TO KEEP” with a heart emoji.
The fallout has resulted in something of an online between the DeadByDaylight community and fans of TheBurntPeanut, many of whom have been attacking players with abusive content and slurs.
Behaviour Interactive initially responded with a statement on its DbD Pulse news account, saying the team member gave the DLC away without approval and that their follow-up comments didn’t fit with the game’s values.
“This weekend, a Dead by Daylight team member awarded in-game content and currency to a creator streaming our game,” the initial statement read.
“Although it is not unusual to unlock content to give creators discovering DbD a chance to have a sneak peek at available content, this decision was made without receiving appropriate approvals. Furthermore, the team member’s subsequent comments and conduct do not align with Dead by Daylight’s core values.
“When concerns about this decision became apparent during the stream, we should have responded by looking into these concerns, not dismissing them.
“Unfortunately, we’ve now seen the fallout of this decision unfolding in many conversations across the DbD community. We appreciate and stand with our community’s willingness to ensure our shared values are being upheld, at all times, regardless of popularity, and we’re heartbroken at the inflammatory language now being directed towards our community.”
This weekend, a Dead by Daylight team member awarded in-game content and currency to a creator streaming our game. Although it is not unusual to unlock content to give creators discovering DbD a chance to have a sneak peek at available content, this decision was made without…
Now the studio has posted a much longer statement on the main Dead by Daylight account on X, going into more detail on what happened and what it’s currently doing.
“The reason this happened is initially very straightforward,” the longer statement said. “Members of our team saw a very large audience appear in the DbD Twitch directory watching a streamer who has not played DbD before.
“Moments like this are usually exciting for the dev team, as they are a chance to welcome new players. But we moved too fast and there were problems with how this played out.”
“The decision was made to give that creator in-game content and directly participate in their chat, before taking the necessary time to look at if this was a good idea. This happened quickly and outside of our usual team discussions.
“When collaborating with a new creator, we normally look thoroughly at their past content to determine whether they are representing the values of inclusion our community expects from us. In this case, this was not taken into proper consideration or discussed as a group.”
Noting that the studio doesn’t have “stringent enough processes” for due diligence on streamers, the statement pointed out when TheBurntPeanut was “seemingly self-aware of the blowback to come” and offered to give back the DLC, the “WE CAN TAKE THE HEAT” response “showed a disregard for the context we were suddenly in and crossed the line of appropriate responses from our brand”.
“That reply escalated the situation for us and for our community, especially our content creators on the frontlines of these conversations, and that’s unacceptable,” it added.
To our community: We wanted to follow up on yesterday’s message to better address the questions you are actually asking and that matter most to you. pic.twitter.com/OPqAJ9xIoh
The studio has now removed the DLC that was granted to the creator, and says it is now “rewriting our guidelines for how we interact with creators playing Dead by Daylight, including who on our team can make those calls. These guidelines will focus on identifying creators whose past conduct has been in direct opposition to the inclusive community we are trying to build.”
“We are updating our request and approval methods for granting content and currency to players,” it said. “While ensuring this updated process involves the proper checks and balances at the right time, it also must take our values into account. We will also be training our team on these new processes and methods to ensure everyone is on the same page.”
Although players appear to have decided that they know which team member was responsible, Behaviour did not identify them in their statement, and said it would be dealing with the matter in private.
“We take this situation very seriously and are taking appropriate action internally,” it explained. “As this is a confidential matter, we won’t be sharing further details.”
The studio now finds itself in an unenviable position where it’s receiving criticism from both sides – Dead by Daylight fans are angry at the way the studio seemingly embraced the streamer while dismissing the criticism that would come, and fans of TheBurntPeanut are now angry at the studio for removing his DLC and attempting to distance itself from him.
“This incident has broken trust with our community who hold expectations and regards for the types of people we partner with, but more importantly expectations of the conduct and actions taken by our team in our daily work within this community,” the studio’s statement concluded. “We understand it will be a slow road to regain that trust but we are committed to doing the work necessary to get there.”

articles.title_orig: How common are national exit taxes?
articles.title_zh: How common are national exit taxes?
articles.content_orig:
Matthew Field is a Senior Technology Reporter covering the UK tech sector. He has covered social media giants, technology policy and British start-ups for The Telegraph since 2017. He also writes about the space industry. He can be reached at matthew.field@telegraph.co.uk or via X @matthfield
Rich residents of Italy who move abroad are to be hit with an “exit tax” under plans drawn up by Giorgia Meloni’s government .
In its draft 2027 budget, Rome said it was planning a 26pc capital gains levy for individuals who move their tax residence abroad and have assets of more than €800,000 (£670,000).
The surprise policy, which was not trailed in advance, threatens to ensnare wealthy British expats and others who have relocated to Italy in recent years.
Some 3,600 millionaires moved to Italy in 2025, according to data from Henley & Partners, putting it behind only the US and the United Arab Emirates as a destination for the wealthy.
The rich have been attracted by Italy’s low taxes on global wealth and the lifestyle offered in cities including Milan and regions such as the Italian Riviera and the Amalfi Coast.
A number of high-profile figures have moved from Britain to Italy in recent years, including Natalia Grosvenor, the Duchess of Westminster; Richard Gnodde, one of London’s top bankers at Goldman Sachs; Nassef Sawiris, the billionaire Aston Villa co-owner; and Thor Björgólfsson , an investor known as Iceland’s first billionaire.
Many were motivated by recent tax changes in the UK, including the scrapping of non-dom status. Mr Björgólfsson, who relocated to Milan, called the number of wealthy entrepreneurs leaving Britain “an exodus”.
Ironically, fears of an exit tax in Britain were what motivated some to leave.
La Repubblica reported that the new Italian exit tax would fall on individuals who had been residents of the country for six out of the ten preceding years.
Italy had previously sought to attract wealthy émigrés by introducing a €100,000 flat tax on foreign income in 2017.
However, Ms Meloni’s Right-wing government doubled this tax in 2024 amid a mounting public backlash, before raising it to €300,000 earlier this year .
A wave of strikes and anti-government protests is currently sweeping more than 40 Italian cities, motivated by cost of living concerns. It mirrors widespread demonstrations and rioting in France.
Ms Meloni faces an election in 2027 after gaining power in 2022. While the prime minister’s ruling Brothers of Italy party is ahead in the polls, its support has been slipping.
Many other countries impose an exit tax on capital gains when wealthy individuals leave. France, for example, imposes an exit tax on those with a net worth of more than €800,000, levied at 31.4pc. A US exit tax hits those worth more than $2m when they give up their citizenship or green card.
Around 66,000 Britons live in Italy. Some 60pc are aged 55 or older, according to data from the British embassy in Rome.
Rachel Reeves, the former chancellor, previously considered introducing an exit tax in the UK. However, the idea was scrapped over fears it would prompt an exodus of millionaires. Economists point out that the levy can backfire and drive people away unless it comes into force immediately after being announced.

articles.title_orig: The 5 most brutal political moggings of 2026
articles.title_zh: The 5 most brutal political moggings of 2026
articles.content_orig:
The Collins English Dictionary announced its 2026 word of the year Tuesday morning, with judges opting for “mogging.”
For readers not fluent in youth culture: Mogging “might involve making [anyone] look inferior in terms of appearance, confidence or status — anything, really,” according to marketing consultant and copywriter Rachel Quin, who authored a Collins article announcing the winner.
According to Collins, the term originated in the bodybuilding community as a shortening of AMOG (“alpha male of the group”) and penetrated into the so-called manosphere , a collection of typically online male communities united by their beliefs about masculinity.
“Fast forward to 2026 and it’s everywhere,” Quin added. And, crucially for POLITICO’s purposes, it can be applied to literally any situation.
With that in mind, we looked back at five top political moggings in 2026 — the more brutal, the better.
One minute, Keir Starmer was British prime minister with a thumping Labour majority cheering his every move. The next, he was humiliated and ousted by a northern rival who had done little to hide his own leadership ambitions.
Starmer, of course, tried to block the Downing Street takeover by Manchester Mayor Andy Burnham.
But once Burnham loyalists and grumpy ministers had quit Starmer’s government in droves, the prime minister bowed out this summer after just two years in office and Burnham — having manufactured, at the second attempt, an opportunity to enter parliament — waltzed into the top job unopposed.
Call it the textbook framemog.
Mozambique’s towering president, Daniel Chapo — who stands more than two meters tall — loomed over tiny Russian leader Vladimir Putin at a summit between African countries and Russia in Moscow last week.
Countries signed a summit declaration pledging to expand “cooperation in energy, minerals, and digital technology, establishing Russian industrial zones in Africa, and localizing production” — but the defining image of the summit was a photo of Chapo dwarfing Putin .
Looksmaxxing influencer Clavicular, real name Braden Peters, likely breathed a sigh of relief, having suffered the year’s other most notorious framemogging, at the hands of internet character ”ASU frat leader.”
In a classic case of nominative determinism, Jacob Rees-Mogg, former British government minister and current haunted pencil, pantsed American commentator Tucker Carlson in a discussion on the latter’s YouTube channel in October.
Rees-Mogg may not have expected to find himself defending Britain’s decision to fight against Adolf Hitler, but that’s what happened after Carlson questioned why Britain had even bothered entering World War II against Nazi Germany.
Rees-Mogg said he was very surprised that Carlson was “verging on defending Hitler,” adding: “I think this is not really what you want to be doing,” in a clip that went viral and catapulted the Brexit hard-liner back into the British public consciousness.
Donald Trump’s bid to clean out the iconic Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool in Washington, D.C. was initially hampered by persistent pond scum.
After a money-spinning renovation in early summer, algae came back with a vengeance, turning the water green and murky, while the blue paint job began to peel off the pool bottom.
Rather than turn his ire toward the contractors, Trump blamed vandals for attacking the pool, and his Department of Justice attempted to prosecute people it accused of damaging the site. Judges, however, dropped or dismissed the criminal cases.
Trump returned to the theme Monday — right before America went to the polls for midterm elections in which the country is laser-focused on the surging cost of living and corruption — holding a rally in front of the pool and recounting all the issues he said he’d fixed with the pool, including “tremendous algae.”
In Hungary’s biggest aura battle ever , conservative challenger Péter Magyar defeated longtime nationalist leader Viktor Orbán, ending 16 years in power for the populist prime minister.
Magyar, a former MP for Orbán’s Fidesz party, dramatically broke ranks in 2024, releasing a tape of his ex-wife apparently incriminating members of Orbán’s inner circle in a corruption scandal when she was justice minister. For two years, he consistently attacked Fidesz and Orbán over graft while building a movement to take down the EU’s problem child.
Magyar ultimately led a big-tent campaign focusing on cost-of-living concerns and pro-EU messaging, which turned into a landslide election victory that left Trump and the Kremlin salty .

articles.title_orig: MTA should eliminate some jobs to prepare for budget woes, watchdog writes
articles.title_zh: MTA should eliminate some jobs to prepare for budget woes, watchdog writes
articles.content_orig:
Make your contribution now and help Gothamist thrive in 2026. Donate today
Gothamist is funded by sponsors and member donations
In less than four years, the MTA could be looking at a nearly $900 million funding shortfall as spending outpaces fare revenue, according to a new analysis from the Citizens Budget Commission, which recommends cutting the workforce to close the gap.
The budget watchdog recommends sweeping job cuts to positions that it argues technology has made obsolete. The budget commission suggested the MTA allow its trains to run with just one worker, instead of two.
Train lines that have new computer-based signals, like the L and the 7, are already fully automated, as are the announcements on the trains. While the conductor opens and closes the train doors, the operator has few other duties, which include hitting a button every 20 seconds to signal they are alert. The budget commission cited the operator’s limited responsibilities as a sign the job could be cut with no impact to service.
Eliminating operator jobs on the L and 7 lines could save $36.5 million a year, according to the report . If the agency moved to phase out two people operating trains across the system, it could save $500 million a year.
The agency is in the process of installing new signals on other lines like the A, C, E, F, G, M and R lines. For now, those lines still require two people to run the trains.
The suggestion from the Citizens Budget Commission comes at a sensitive time as Transport Workers Union Local 100 negotiates a contract with the MTA for its 40,000 subway and bus workers. The MTA is expected to release its financial plan for next year in the coming weeks, which will include a 4% fare and toll increase. The board will vote on that plan in December.
“The same recommendations have been coming down for dozens of years, so there's nothing new about it,” said Transport Workers Union of America President John Samuelsen. “It's essentially a recommendation to balance alleged deficits that the MTA has off the backs of working people.”
Last year, the state legislature tried to enshrine a requirement of two MTA workers on each train into law, but Gov. Kathy Hochul vetoed the bill , leaving open the possibility that one-person train operations could happen in the future.
“Legislatively mandated staffing prevents the MTA from modernizing — as technology and best practices continue to improve — and realizing the efficiency and financial benefits,” the Citizens Budget Commission's report argues.
The Citizens Budget Commission acknowledges the MTA has become more efficient in recent years, saving a reported $576 million this year through what the agency calls “operating efficiencies.” But the report argues that without cutting labor and healthcare costs, the MTA faces a $300 million budget gap next year that will grow to $900 million by 2030. The budget commission estimates its recommended reforms could save $2.5 billion annually.
Other recommendations include streamlining fare collection on the commuter railroads by checking tickets prior to boarding, reducing the need for someone to walk through the train. The Citizens Budget Commission argues cutting more than 1,000 jobs on Metro-North and the Long Island Rail Road could save $380 million annually.
The report also recommended MTA retirees pay more in healthcare premiums, which could bring in an additional $315 million a year.
Samuelsen countered that many laborers, ironworkers, track workers, and crane operators in the MTA get paid less than their peers in the private sector, but accept that because of the generous retirement benefits.
"The CBC is right to note that we've made extraordinary progress in securing hundreds of millions of dollars in new recurring operational efficiencies," MTA spokesperson Mitch Schwartz wrote in a statement. He did not address the proposal to eliminate jobs.
Stephen Nessen covers transportation. Since 2008 he has reported on everything from Occupy Wall Street, the rebuilding of the World Trade Center site, Hurricane Sandy, to Trump’s campaign for president. articles.title_zh: Shopify Stock Plunges. Slowing Merchandise Sales Flash a Warning Sign.
articles.content_orig:
Shares of e-commerce platform Shopify fell 7% on Tuesday after the company missed estimates on subscription gross profit and gross merchandise volume.
Shopify reported before the bell Tuesday and posted adjusted earnings of 49 cents per share, topping LSEG estimates of 46 cents per share.
Overall, quarterly revenue of $3.74 billion came in just below LSEG estimates of $3.75 billion. Shopify said it sees revenue growth in the "low thirties" range year over year for the fourth quarter, versus LSEG estimates of 32.1%.
Gross merchandise volume, which came in at $119.15 billion, missed analyst estimates of $120.03 billion for the quarter, according to StreetAccount. Subscription gross profit also missed estimates by nearly $20 million, coming in at $661 million compared to StreetAccount estimates of $680.3 million. Merchant gross profit beat estimates.
Shopify president Harley Finkelstein called the GMV results "consistent" and "durable" in comments to CNBC's "Squawk on the Street" on Tuesday, and noted it was the thirteenth consecutive quarter of GMV growth above 20%.
"We're really proud of the print, and we're going to keep building for the long term and ignore the noise day to day," Finkelstein said.
Subscription revenue of $836 million also missed analyst estimates of $848.1 million, according to FactSet. Merchant revenue beat estimates.

articles.title_orig: 5 iPhone Features You Should Be Using After Updating To iOS 27
articles.title_zh: 5 iPhone Features You Should Be Using After Updating To iOS 27
articles.content_orig:
iOS 27 just made your iPhone a lot more capable.
The iPhone is easy to recommend to anyone looking for great smartphone hardware and long-term software support. The previous few iOS releases, however, have been pretty janky. With iOS 27, Apple therefore shifted its focus to ironing out bugs and improving overall stability rather than cramming in another round of flashy new features, and a good chunk of the WWDC 2026 keynote covered improvements such as snappier app launch times, faster AirDrop transfers and better memory management.
Apple's commitment to software updates also means iOS 27 compatibility extends all the way back to the iPhone 11, which is great news since iOS 26 would have been a terrible final major update to be stuck on. If you haven't already updated your iPhone, you can do so by navigating to Settings > General > Software Update .
Not much has changed visually, which makes sense since Apple only recently overhauled its design language with Liquid Glass. There is now a system-wide transparency slider, though, which many users had been asking about. Reports about battery life are mixed — some say they're getting less screen-on time than before, while others haven't had issues. Personally, iOS 27 has been such a blessing performance-wise on my aging iPhone 15 Pro Max that I'm willing to put up with slightly worse battery life.
Of course, stability upgrades aren't the only thing Apple introduced with iOS 27. The update also brings a handful of useful tidbits, and here are five features you should definitely check out after updating your iPhone.
Apple Intelligence has had a rocky start. After all, it took Apple two whole iOS generations to deliver on its promises of a more capable Siri. Most of the Apple Intelligence suite has been pretty underwhelming, unless you're one of the five people who enjoy generating custom emojis using Genmoji , but iOS 27 changes that. The Shortcuts app has received a major upgrade, and Apple Intelligence might finally have a genuinely useful feature to show for itself.
You've been able to create pretty complex shortcuts and automations on iOS for a while now, and you can even import shortcuts that others have created and shared. iOS 27 now lets you create shortcuts using natural language prompts, which Apple Intelligence handles. When you launch the app and tap the + button, you can start describing the shortcut you want.
In my testing, the integration works pretty well and usually creates straightforward shortcuts without issues. That said, it pieces together the wrong actions sometimes and ends up with a shortcut that doesn't do exactly what you want. Fortunately, you can still manually tweak shortcuts created using Apple Intelligence by tapping Edit .
You can also use Apple Intelligence actions within your shortcuts. Apple currently offers three AI models, including an on-device model for faster processing. You can create shortcuts for actions involving information extraction, summarization or generation of text and documents. The Cloud and Cloud Pro models do have a daily rate limit, though.
The Wallet app on the iPhone stores your payment cards, transit passes, event and cinema tickets, digital keys and more. Until now, users could only add digital passes and credentials if the issuer supported Apple Wallet and provided a compatible pass. While several companies and services offered this convenience, plenty of issuers didn't support it. As a collector, I was a bit disheartened to see my local IMAX theater stop offering Apple Wallet passes for movie tickets.
With iOS 27, you can create custom passes and add them to Apple Wallet. This is extremely handy for those with loyalty cards or gym memberships that don't offer native Apple Wallet support. There are two ways you can create a pass in Apple Wallet, and Apple Intelligence comes in handy again here. On supported iPhone models, you can open an image (or screenshot) of a ticket or membership card with a barcode, swipe up and tap on Add Pass to Wallet .
If this option doesn't show up, you can also open the Wallet app, tap the + icon at the top and select Create a Pass . Tap on Continue and take a photo of the ticket or ID card. The Wallet app will then use Visual Intelligence to extract relevant information from the image and create a pass. If you want to change the pass' details or visuals, tap Edit.
For years, Apple's virtual assistant, Siri, has lagged behind competitors like Google Assistant. Slow responses are forgivable, but Siri would often struggle with even the most basic requests. Apple first promised a major Siri overhaul with iOS 18's Apple Intelligence suite, but it's taken over two years to come to fruition. iOS 27 comes with Siri AI , and users with a compatible iPhone can join the waitlist by navigating to Settings > Siri . The AI-powered virtual assistant is still in beta, but things are already starting to look promising.
Siri now understands and fulfills your requests noticeably better, with a huge improvement in how it handles follow-up queries. Though it still takes a hot second to process most requests, its responses are more relevant, and it doesn't hit you with the "Here's what I found on the web" reply as often. What's more impressive about Siri AI, though, is the fact that it now understands personal context.
It can pull information from your messages, emails, photos and more to answer questions or perform tasks that previously required you to manually dig through different apps. Third-party app support is still limited, but if you mainly use iMessage and the default Mail app on your iPhone, you'll likely find Siri to be one of iOS 27's biggest improvements. The Camera app has a new Siri mode as well, which taps into Visual Intelligence to answer questions about whatever you're pointing your camera at.
The AirPods are some of the most popular wireless earbuds on the market, and they work best when paired with an iPhone, iPad or Mac. Most modern AirPods models support Spatial Audio with head tracking, and several music streaming services like Apple Music and Tidal let you enjoy Dolby Atmos content. Sound quality is also widely regarded as one of their strongest selling points, particularly on the higher-end Pro models like the AirPods Pro 3 that we reviewed. With iOS 27, though, you can finally tweak the sound to your liking using a built-in equalizer.
Apps like Apple Music have long allowed you to apply EQ presets, but the new AirPods equalizer works system-wide. The feature is available on AirPods 4 and newer, AirPods Pro 2 and newer and the AirPods Max 2. Connect your AirPods to your iPhone, launch the Settings app, tap on the AirPods settings at the top of the screen and navigate to Audio & Routing > Equalizer .
The Recommended option is selected by default, which delivers the balanced sound profile you've grown used to. If you tap on Custom , you can manually adjust the lows, mids and highs to your liking. If you prefer thumpy bass, increase the lows slider, but if you want vocals to sound clearer, try bumping up the mids or highs instead. Though Apple is only offering a 3-band equalizer, it's still a welcome addition. My AirPods Pro 2 already deliver punchy lows, but as a basshead, I appreciate having the option to crank up the bass even further.
Apple's latest mobile OS also has several additions that make browsing more convenient. For starters, Safari now lets you set up alerts for webpage changes, so you don't have to check yourself. This is useful if you're tracking a product's price, waiting for tickets to go on sale or keeping an eye on when an out-of-stock item becomes available again.
On your iPhone, launch Safari , head to a webpage you want to track, tap on the icon with three horizontal lines in the address bar and select Notify Me . Since this feature uses Apple Intelligence, you can describe what exactly you want Safari to monitor. You can then choose how frequently Safari checks the webpage for changes.
Safar

articles.title_orig: Apple explains the $400 premium for the MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display
articles.title_zh: Apple explains the $400 premium for the MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display
articles.content_orig:
Apple argued that the touchscreen isn’t the headline feature of the MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display , merely a bonus.
The headline should instead be the quality of the display itself – with the company effectively suggesting that the $400 premium is positively cheap for what you’re getting …
Apple published a white paper in which it argues that the latest MacBook Pro display is essentially a smaller version of its professional reference monitor, the Studio Display XDR .
Given that this costs anywhere from $2,899 to $3,599 just for a display (albeit a significantly larger one with a correspondingly higher resolution), this does put into perspective that $400 extra over the MacBook Pro with the standard screen. Here’s what Apple has to say about it:
PROLED XDR display, the best display in a pro laptop, finally overcomes these historic limitations. For the first time, a MacBook Pro display uses tandem OLED technology, delivering up to 1000 nits of sustained full-screen brightness, 2000 nits of peak high dynamic range (HDR) and standard dynamic range (SDR) brightness, and a 10,000,000:1 contrast ratio with accurate, per-pixel black levels.
It’s driven in real time by an all-new display engine in M5 Pro and M5 Max, which continuously compensates each pixel for content, usage, temperature, and ambient conditions—delivering creative precision out of the box and protecting panel lifespan over time. And a unique manufacturing process ensures panel-to-panel consistency and minimizes off-axis color shift, a first for any OLED laptop.
As Macworld spotted, that’s almost identical to the company’s description of the the Studio Display XDR.
In fact, the PROLED XDR in the MacBook Pro is the only display other than the Studio Display XDR that supports Apple CMF 2026, the next generation of CIE 1931. Apple says CMF 2026 “more precisely aligns the appearance of the display with an ideal D65 illuminant—the standard reference for white—and significantly improves appearance matching across display technologies, which is important for workflows that use multiple displays side by side.”
Resolution aside, the other specs are identical with just one exception: the contrast ratio. As for that exception, the MacBook display comes out on top with a 10 million to 1 contrast ratio, in contrast with the Studio Display XDR’s one million.
Does this change your own perspective of the price premium of the OLED model? Please share your thoughts in the comments.

articles.title_orig: Xbox's New 25 Years Bundle Retails For $569.99, And Here's The Full List Of Games
articles.title_zh: Xbox's New 25 Years Bundle Retails For $569.99, And Here's The Full List Of Games
articles.content_orig:
Last week, you may recall that we ran a story about how Xbox was giving away 25 free games to eligible buyers of Windows 11 PCs , and that the offer was technically supposed to begin on November 2nd (but had begun slightly early).
Well, last night, the "25 Years of XBOX Bundle" suddenly appeared on the Microsoft Store with an actual price tag, meaning that even if you aren't eligible to get the games for free, you can actually buy the bundle if you really want to.
Just one problem - it's retailing for a whopping $569.99.
Its existence on the Microsoft Store also means we have the full list of included games, which is as follows:
Now, as much as there are some excellent games in the list here, it's hard to recommend paying anywhere near $569.99 for them. We reckon that's not really the point though — the bundle was created as a generous freebie for new Windows 11 PC buyers after all. It's also only available in the United States.
Should you wish to go ahead and get it anyway, you'll obviously be able to play all 25 of them on PC, while around half include the Xbox One / Series X|S versions via Play Anywhere, such as Gears of War: Reloaded and DOOM + DOOM 2 .
We reckon it's only worth picking up if you fall into the "eligible" freebie bracket, which unfortunately still remains quite vague when looking at the official FAQ for the 25 years of XBOX bundle .
"Customers in the United States are eligible when they purchase and activate a qualifying new Windows PC from a participating U.S. retailer or OEM during the offer period. Eligible devices include select Windows Home PCs from participating Microsoft and OEM device lines, including qualifying handhelds. The only Windows Pro exception is a qualifying NVIDIA RTX Spark™ devices running Windows Pro. Other Windows Pro devices are not eligible. The offer is valid for qualifying purchases made between November 2, 2026, at 12:00 AM UTC and December 31, 2026, at 11:59 PM UTC, while supplies last."
We've already seen some people getting the bundle for free after buying a ROG Xbox Ally X20 in recent days, so that handheld seems to be part of the promotion, but it'd be nice if we had a proper breakdown of all the eligible devices.
Anyway, let us know what you think about this bundle in the comments down below - are you hoping to claim yours?!

articles.title_orig: Google Will Turn Off Search for Schools That Reject A.I.
articles.title_zh: Google Will Turn Off Search for Schools That Reject A.I.
articles.content_orig:
Google said AI is built into Search and cannot be switched off, leaving schools that want no AI without Search access
David Paul Morris/Bloomberg via Getty Images
Google $GOOGL is telling school districts that want no AI on school devices that they must give up Google Search, according to Chalkbeat .
Google on Tuesday announced changes to its school products , including Guided Learning features in Search and Google Classroom and a new approach to school controls. The company said access to Gemini, Gemini Notebook, Gemini in Classroom and Google Search will be off for K-12 student accounts until school administrators turn them on. Google said it will share specifics with schools in the coming months, ahead of the rollout.
"If a school is not comfortable with that and simply wants AI off, then they have the choice to not have Search on at all," Chris Phillips, Google 's vice president and general manager of education, said, according to Chalkbeat. Phillips described AI as so thoroughly woven into Search that it can't be switched off.
Phillips also told The New York Times that students at schools that ban AI "will not have access to search, and they'll see a message from their school that indicates it's not available."
Google said the Guided Learning feature in Search is meant for student accounts and walks students through homework problems step by step instead of giving the answer directly. The company will start with a pilot in select U.S. schools later this month, then expand to other districts in the coming months. Guided Learning also became available globally in Google Classroom on Tuesday, where teachers can assign activities and see real-time insights on where a class needs support.
Guided Learning will take the place of AI Overviews for students who search while signed in to school accounts, according to Chalkbeat. Chalkbeat also reported that Google intends to pilot the changes in a handful of U.S. schools this month, with a wider rollout set for early next year.
Eisha Bush, head of teaching and learning at the advocacy group Common Sense Media, said it is “slim to none” that schools and students will steer clear of Google Search, according to Chalkbeat. Google has also never let schools disable AI Overviews, and getting rid of AI Mode has meant working around it with tricky technical fixes. Common Sense Media’s Youth AI Safety Institute has labeled both AI Overviews and AI Mode in Search an “unacceptable risk” to students, according to Chalkbeat.
The changes arrive as parents press for greater control over school technology and as big districts, including New York and Los Angeles, impose heavy limits on how students can use AI, according to Chalkbeat.

articles.title_orig: Beyond screens: Mercedes-Benz’s new holographic heads-up display
articles.title_zh: Beyond screens: Mercedes-Benz’s new holographic heads-up display
articles.content_orig:
Do screens in cars represent luxury? Judging by the latest car interiors, the answer would seem to be an emphatic “yes.” Screens aren’t just getting larger; they are multiplying across the dashboard and morphing into different forms and concepts. Indeed, an interior’s screens are a pretty good indicator of what brand made the car—or at least how much the owner paid for it.
But is this actually what customers want ? Are more screens really better? And even if they are, luxury car features inevitably trickle down to cheaper, more mainstream offerings, and screens can only get so big. That leaves luxury automakers with another question to answer: “What’s next?”
Mercedes-Benz is working on a new display alternative that could provide an answer. For now, it’s known as the holographic display. Forget the images from Star Trek and Star Wars that just popped into your head, though. It’s effectively a more advanced form of heads-up display, or HUD.
Whereas a traditional HUD projects images onto the windshield glass, the holographic display has two main components. It still uses a projector, but its key element is a special transparent film laminated into the glass. The film uses holographic optical elements, or “super-small mirrors,” as Mercedes development engineer Lena Hees described them, that selectively reflect the light emitted by the projector, keeping the image visible even in direct sunlight while hiding it from the driver’s view.
Today, the passenger-side touchscreens in Mercedes and other luxury vehicles rely on driver-monitoring cameras or screen polarization to keep the driver from seeing what is playing on the passenger side.
Speaking of passenger screens, the holographic display is clearly being considered as a future alternative or replacement for this technology. Although screens in cars are increasingly ubiquitous, a recent JD Power study indicated that car owners classify passenger screens as “ not necessary ” and have generally negative opinions about them. Mercedes has clearly observed similar opinions but for slightly different reasons.
“We have customers who like the Hyperscreen,” said development engineer Maximilian Hilger of the pillar-to-pillar screen found in an increasing number of Mercedes models. “But there are others who want to maintain luxury materials.”
In other words, the massive screen design doesn’t seem as luxurious as the pillar-to-pillar bands of wood or other materials found in previous-generation models. And that’s not an opinion isolated to Mercedes’ customers.
New Mercedes chief design officer Bastian Baudy recently told German magazine Auto Motor Sport that “Materiality and haptics must remain tangible—with switches, buttons, and intuitive controls. Real materials are at the heart of Mercedes: metal, wood.”
Mercedes CEO Ola Källenius went further, grouping interior quality and materials among the brand’s “forever values,” along with safety and maintaining what a Mercedes is like to drive.
That presents conflicting priorities, however.
“Yes, you need to have all the [technology] that a customer could ever dream of and wants,” Källenius told Ars. “But you need to package it in an aesthetically pleasing way. That’s also part of it.”
That brings us back to the holographic display. Keep in mind that the photos in this article show early prototypes I saw at Mercedes’ research facilities in Sindelfingen, Germany. The prototype projector sits inside a rather crude, trapezoidal hole dug into the dash of a right-hand-drive, pre-2027 S-Class. It’s also loud, with a cooling fan whirring like a laptop visiting too many junk-filled websites.
The production version would have a much smaller projector opening than those of the prototype and existing heads-up displays. Manual Holstein, a manager working in Mercedes research for future displays, indicated that the projector could be small enough to be hidden behind wood or metal trim pieces. Holstein also said you won’t hear a fan in the production model and that the resolution would improve.
The resolution is certainly considerably better than any current head-up display, including Mercedes’ own, which features augmented reality elements . Full-color, commercial-like videos of the C-Class Electric played during the demonstration, and the display was sufficiently bright, even though Holstein said the prototype was operating at just 20 percent of its maximum brightness.
Issues remain, however. The resolution may be good compared to the arrows, script, and graphics of a current HUD, but it’s poor when compared to a passenger touchscreen. The video’s contrast was also too high, and as you can see in the photos, the picture was distorted into a narrow height due to the angle of the windshield. Frankly, no one would choose to watch anything on it over a phone, tablet, or conventional passenger screen. It needs to improve by orders of magnitude before becoming a viable alternative.
Again, though, this is just a prototype. Holstein said the holographic film size, or “eyebox,” can be made much bigger and be raised higher than the HUD-like height of the prototype. He also dismissed the distortion as a problem unique to the prototype.
Imagine nearly half the windshield transformed into a virtual screen that’s visible only to the passenger. Beyond videos or other entertainment, Mercedes envisions the holographic display highlighting points of interest in the view through the windshield. A similar display could be placed on the driver side, showing situational information, enabling video calls, or providing entertainment when parked. In the future, it could even let drivers watch things other than the road when Mercedes’ Level 3 autonomous driving system allows them to take their eyes off it. At the very least, the technology could replace today’s HUDs and their larger projector boxes.
Having experienced the prototype while the car was moving, I also think the holographic display could help prevent the motion sickness that can come from staring at a passenger screen while the car is moving. The higher screen angle and ability to see more of the outside world beyond created a notably different visual experience.
Of course, the question remains: “Is this what customers want?”
If the JD Power survey found that customers don’t care about passenger touchscreens, will they be any more enthusiastic about holographic video displays? That seems doubtful. But that’s just as much of an open question as whether the production version will actually live up to its promises.
There’s also another matter: What, exactly, defines luxury? Before Bastian Baudy took over as Mercedes’ chief design officer this year, his predecessor and former boss Gordon Wagener echoed Källenius’ thoughts about the direction of the brand’s interiors. He was considerably blunter, though.
“Screens are not luxury,” Wagener told ABC News . “You have a better—and bigger—TV at home, right? And every car has a big screen. So we have to create luxury beyond the screen. That’s why I talk about craftsmanship and sophistication.”
If the holographic display lets automakers emphasize traditional design and materials while still offering unique technology, it could be a promising way forward.

articles.title_orig: World of Warcraft: Forever Is Already Overrun with AI Slop
articles.title_zh: World of Warcraft: Forever Is Already Overrun with AI Slop
articles.content_orig:
World of Warcraft: Forever, a re-imaginging of the legendary MMO, comes out Wednesday. The idea is to recapture the feeling of discovery and wonder players had when adventuring across its world for the first time back in 2004.
But 2026 is a very different time. Subreddits dedicated to the game are already overrun with AI-generated addons that rip off longtime developers’ work, and a company that helps players track their damage output tells me it is making changes to its API because of the inundation of AI slop addons.
Warcraft Logs is a long-running site made by Archon.gg that lets players track and share their logs of particular in-game fights so they can analyze them for ways to get better. This works by players downloading Archon’s software which records the data of their fights and uploads them to the site. Warcraft Logs makes its API available for free to other developers. It used to be mostly hobby developers, the CEO of Archon.gg and Warcraft Logs, who goes by Sildri Silentcrest, told me. Now, it’s increasingly commercial projects, which are supposed to ask for permission in order to head off projects that would break Warcraft Logs’ terms of service or wouldn’t be able to scale.
“There’s been [an] explosion of development,” Silentcrest said. “Now, we’re averaging a[t] least one commercial ask per day. And I’m sure there are more that are commercializing without our approval. One new World of Warcraft analysis company every day! It's hard to keep up.”
At the root of many of these is the explosion of vibe-coded sites and addons. Addons are custom pieces of software a World of Warcraft player loads into their game for a specific benefit. Maybe they want a guide on the most optimal questing path to take, so an addon shows them the way on their minimap; or they want to make big changes to the UI. Some developers make real money from these, either by running Patreons or receiving ad revenue from Curseforge, the main repository for World of Warcraft addons.
If you scrolled any of the World of Warcraft subreddits in the past few weeks, you likely came across someone posting about the new addon they ‘created’. Sometimes the poster discloses they used AI, other times they add an update later after being called out. There’s even a tool for players to use Claude or Codex while they’re in World of Warcraft, so they can keep making addons in the game.
And with the flood, Warcraft Logs is changing its own API. “We're changing our API to better align with the applications we want to enable. We like things that help our community to dive deeper into their data, like tools that give you a deep dive on why you died to a boss or how you can improve on your next attempt. We don’t like things that effectively scrape lots of the data from our site to show surface-level info on their own site. Unfortunately, the ‘scrape and show basic statistics’ type has become much more prevalent,” Silentcrest said. They said Warcraft Logs is also introducing a paid commercial key “so that developers with commercial ambitions can support the foundation for the projects.”
Addons have been a crucial and thriving part of World of Warcraft for essentially the game’s entire life. Developers have spent many, many hours crafting those over the years. Now, AI is ripping those off too.
“People are making rip-offs of my work and copying my ideas,” plusmouse, a well-known addon creator , told me. Plusmouse gave one example: a particular design for nameplates in the game, which are the bars that appear above an enemy’s head.
“Prior to that releasing I hadn’t seen any addons adopt that style of design, and now, it feels like every AI addon ends up using that idea,” they said. Plusmouse has found in some cases the code is so similar in the AI-generated versions, that they submit copyright complaints to Curseforge. “Sometimes the code is so similar the complaint results in a takedown, other times it’s just different enough to get away with it, despite feeling like my solution. Borrowing ideas is normal in addon development, but doing it on the scale that AI permits isn’t,” they said. Plusmouse said they made some of their GitHub repositories private, which they believe has stopped LLMs from using their code.
Another key part of World of Warcraft: Forever is that the game is letting players engage with it in their own, preferred way.
“If I can be hopeful, the ubiquity of services under development will allow people to pick their own experience,” Silvercrest added. “If they want to take their time and explore in a relaxed manner, then they can. If they have limited time and want to get to endgame content quickly, they can do that too. On the flip side, my worry is that there will be lots of abandonware that will frustrate users with out-of-date information, buggy software, and vulnerabilities.”
Silvercrest said staff at Warcraft Logs “feel pressure to do more,” and the site has used some AI itself for research and some code review. “We have a small team. People are using our API to vibecode features that are on our own to do list. Should we take those features off our list? Or should we bite the bullet and lean into AI tools ourselves?”
They added, “Two years ago, say we had 200 developers using our API and two or three or four were being abusive. Today, 10,000 developers are using our API and 1,000 are being abusive. The ratio has changed, and that really feels bad. It used [to] be developers respecting other developers’ hard work. I'm not sure what’s changed. Is it that Claude doesn’t read the ToS? Or is it that the new developers don’t care as much as the old? We seriously love some of the tools that this coding accessibility has enabled, but policing API use has become a struggle.”
